role.altitude: The specialist stops building Excel extracts and grading jobs one at a time. They own the job architecture and the evidence for every pay difference ahead of the first pay transparency report (2027 pay, due 7 June 2028). They decide which differences are explained, which go to the works council, and when a role has changed enough to regrade.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: co-own the governed AFAS pay extract and gap model; learn the data model and its tests.
Payroll Specialist: check grade and scale changes before month close; learn the CAO scale tables and payroll cut-off.
HR Business Partner: prepare calibration and pay-request answers for managers; learn operational context per site.
FP&A Analyst: cost merit and CAO scenarios; learn the budget model and accruals.
skills_to_grow: Job evaluation on the four pay transparency factors (skills, responsibilities, effort, working conditions)
Reading and testing a deterministic pay-gap model, including agency worker pay data
Checking model-drafted text and grade reasons, and keeping AI Act logs
Preparing works council consent dossiers under WOR 27(1)(c)
Basic SQL and Power BI on the AFAS extract
role.ambitious_version: An always-current pay gap and band position view per job group, site and gender, including flex workers. Pay requests are answered from it within days instead of two months. Every gap above 5% has a written explanation or remediation plan before the works council asks.

tasks.short: Design and revise pay, promotion and appraisal methods, test their effects, and explain them to managers and staff.

steps.what: Pull salary, grade, promotion, offer and training data into Excel
Analyse how current methods work: offer acceptance, promotion rates, raises by group
Draft a revised method: merit matrix, promotion criteria, job evaluation factors

loop.input: Current policy, CAO clauses, effect analysis and the specialist's chosen options
loop.output: Draft policy text with a change log against the current version
loop.check: Specialist reads every clause; a deterministic check confirms cited CAO articles and scale numbers exist in the source
loop.stop: One draft plus up to two revisions per request; otherwise the specialist writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy text must be written from free-text sources and options; templates alone do not cover new methods

steps.what: Consult HR director, HRBPs and works council; adjust the proposal
Write manager guides and staff explanations; publish on SharePoint

loop.output: Plain-language manager guide and staff notice in Dutch
loop.check: Specialist reviews; a diff confirms every number in the guide matches the policy
loop.stop: One draft per audience; fallback to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewriting policy into plain language for different readers needs free text generation

tasks.design: A nightly job on a governed data platform joins the AFAS extract already used for Power BI with Recruitee offers and Studytube completions, and feeds a Power BI page showing raises, promotions and offer acceptance per grade, site and gender. A bounded drafting step turns the specialist's chosen options and the CAO text into policy and guide drafts in Word on SharePoint; consultation and consent stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data sat in three systems with no shared key, so each analysis was a one-off Excel job, and drafting policy text had no tool support.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the joined extract and dashboard a days-long build, and language models draft usable policy and guide text from sources the specialist supplies.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the method is a judgement on fairness, cost and CAO limits; works council consent under WOR 27(1)(c) and sector regrading by CAO parties set the pace.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing fairness, cost and workforce reaction, and winning consent from the works council and managers.

ambition.what: Review offer acceptance and promotion outcomes per grade every quarter instead of once a year at the merit round.

tasks.altitude: Fewer hours in Excel, more in design and consultation. The specialist proposes method changes backed by quarterly evidence rather than yearly anecdotes.

reach.learn: Data model, join keys and data tests

reach.task: Explain new methods to site managers
reach.learn: Which manager questions recur and why

evidence.claim: Pay transparency requires job evaluation on four factors and works council consent to the system, criteria and grouping
A pay or grading system needs works council consent unless a CAO settles it
49% of employers say salary structures lag job changes
Language models can draft policy text from supplied sources

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract for Power BI can be reused for this data.
Recruitee and Studytube expose APIs or exports with an employee or candidate key that maps to AFAS.
unknowns: Which methods Noordhaven changes itself versus what the CAOs fix.
Whether the works council has already consented to the current grading system.
research_questions: How many method changes did HR propose in the last two years, and how long did each analysis take?
Can Recruitee offers be linked to AFAS employee numbers without manual matching?
Does the works council accept model-drafted policy text if the change log is shown?

tasks.short: Run the yearly appraisal and merit cycle and check ratings and raises for unequal treatment.

steps.what: Set up appraisal cycle, send forms to managers, chase late ones
Collect ratings and merit proposals from managers in Excel
Check ratings and raises by gender, age, site and contract type
Hold calibration meetings with HRBPs and managers; settle outliers
Report results to HR director and works council; note program changes

tasks.design: Move the appraisal and merit round from mailed Excel files into AFAS Profit workflows and forms, with reminders handled by the workflow. A deterministic job on the AFAS extract computes rating and raise distributions per group and flags outliers in Power BI before calibration, and fills a fixed report template for the HR director and works council. No model is needed at run time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Managers on three sites and shifts worked in mailed spreadsheets, so data arrived late and in different shapes, and equity checks were done by hand at the end.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflows can carry the forms, and AI-assisted coding makes the distribution checks and report template quick to build and test.
tasks.still_hard: Getting shift managers to use the forms on time; calibration is a negotiation; rating data is sensitive and a pay decision may not be made solely by a model (GDPR Art. 22).
tasks.human_edge: Challenging managers in calibration and deciding which outliers are justified.

ambition.what: Run the equity check on every merit proposal as it arrives, so outliers are discussed before calibration rather than after.

tasks.altitude: The chasing and merging disappear. The specialist spends the cycle on calibration and on deciding which differences need correction.

reach.learn: Cut-off dates and how raises flow into the month close

evidence.claim: A gap of 5% or more unexplained after six months triggers a joint evaluation with the works council
Merit and advice work suits a copilot with autonomy 1-2
AFAS Profit supports workflows and forms for HR processes

assumptions: The merit round runs once a year through Excel today.
Managers have AFAS self-service access or can get it.
unknowns: Whether warehouse shift leads can reach AFAS forms on a device during shifts.
Whether the appraisal system already has works council consent and would need it again after the change.
research_questions: How many days of chasing did last year's merit round take?
What share of managers returned forms late or in a changed format?
Does an AFAS workflow license and configuration already exist for HR forms?

tasks.short: Keep job, pay and benefit records in AFAS right, and update the staff handbook and regulations.

steps.what: Enter job, grade, salary and benefit changes in AFAS from mails and forms
Find wrong or missing grades, job schemes and CAO scale mismatches
Update handbook and benefit regulations after CAO or policy changes

loop.input: New CAO or policy text and the current handbook sections
loop.output: Redline of affected sections with source references
loop.check: Specialist approves each change; deterministic check that every amount and date in the redline appears in the source
loop.stop: One pass per changed source document; unmatched sections go to the specialist
loop.why_not_simpler: Finding which handbook passages a CAO change touches requires reading free text

steps.what: Publish the new version and tell staff and managers what changed

tasks.design: Change requests come in through AFAS Profit workflow forms with field validation, so the specialist approves rather than types. A nightly deterministic check on the AFAS extract compares grades and scales with the CAO scale table and the job schemes AFAS Profit 8 stores, and sends an exception list to HR admin. A bounded drafting step turns CAO or policy changes into a handbook redline on SharePoint, with versioned publishing and a change notice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived by mail in free form and the CAO-to-handbook mapping lived in the specialist's head, so checks happened only when payroll errors surfaced.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 has fields for job schemes and categories, AI-assisted coding makes the scale check cheap, and models can map a new CAO text onto handbook sections.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the CAO scale table current while CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties regrade the sector; interpreting ambiguous CAO clauses.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting CAO clauses and deciding how a change applies to edge cases such as part-time shift workers.

ambition.what: A monthly record-quality report to payroll before close, showing every grade and scale mismatch, as a base for the pay transparency report.

tasks.altitude: Record entry becomes approval. The specialist owns record quality as a measured figure rather than fixing errors after payroll finds them.

reach.learn: Which mismatches come from which change type
How record errors show up in pay runs

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency
CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading the sector's jobs with no outcome yet
A wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference

assumptions: Noordhaven runs or will move to AFAS Profit 8.
The handbook lives on SharePoint as Word documents.
unknowns: Who owns the CAO scale table today and how it is kept.
How many record changes the specialist enters per month versus HR admin.
research_questions: How many payroll corrections last year traced back to grade or scale errors?
Are job schemes already filled in AFAS for all jobs?
How long did the last CAO change take to reach the handbook?

tasks.short: Build org charts, career path tables and pay analysis reports on jobs, grades and pay.

steps.what: Extract job, grade, salary and FTE data from AFAS into Excel
Draw org charts and career path tables per job family
Compute compa-ratios, band position and pay gaps by group
Write findings and explanations for gaps

loop.input: Computed gap and band tables plus the specialist's notes on known causes
loop.output: Draft commentary naming the largest differences and possible explanations
loop.check: Every number in the text is matched against the tables by code; specialist approves all explanations
loop.stop: One draft per report; any unmatched number blocks the draft and returns it to the specialist
loop.why_not_simpler: Commentary is free text; but the figures themselves stay deterministic

steps.what: Send report to HR director and HRBPs

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads the nightly AFAS extract, computes band position, compa-ratios and gaps per job group, site and gender, and renders org charts and career path tables; Power BI shows the results with row-level security. A bounded drafting step writes commentary checked number by number, and the report is a live Power BI page instead of a mailed file. The same pipeline produces the yearly pay transparency figures, with agency pay data added from the agency portals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report was rebuilt by hand from fresh Excel extracts, and there was no external deadline that justified a build.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency law sets a fixed yearly report and the AFAS extract already exists; AI-assisted coding makes the pipeline and charts a short build.
tasks.still_hard: Grouping jobs of equal value is a judgement needing works council consent; agency pay data from three agencies arrives in different formats.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which gap explanations hold up and which need correction.

ambition.what: Give each site manager a monthly view of band position for their team, including flex workers, which they have never had.

tasks.altitude: No more report building. The specialist reviews gaps monthly and decides on explanations and remediation instead of producing yearly snapshots.

reach.task: Maintain the AFAS extract and Power BI model

reach.learn: Budget impact of moving people within bands

Gap figures fit deterministic software from AFAS
Compa Analyst Agent with Mercer data drafts market-pricing findings, with no customer result
Grade or pay recommendations can be high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(b)

How many reports of this kind the specialist makes per year and for whom.
